newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-ICI seen hurt by price weakness.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-ICI seen hurt by price weakness.

text.p: Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc is expected to report sharply lower full-year results on Thursday as price pressure continued to hurt the company in the fourth quarter.
Analysts said oil price strength and the pound's recent rise would also have hit trading conditions at Britain's biggest chemical firm.

Their forecasts for full-year pre-tax profit vary between 600 and 650 million stg before exceptional items, down from 951 million in 1995. But industry watchers say better times lie ahead as prices of some products have picked up.
A collapse in key industrial chemicals dragged down ICI results earlier in the year after prices dropped from their peaks reached mid-1995.
But titanium dioxide is recovering and polyester prices seem to have reached their bottom.
The renewed strength in titanium dioxide will probably start to have a positive impact in the second quarter, said Jeremy Chantry, an analyst at Kleinwort Benson.
"There is usually a timelag but that area is definitely improving," he said.
Another analyst, who declined to be named, said the main short-term uncertainty was the strength of the pound against the dollar and the mark, after sterling's recent abrupt retreat from its highs.
Pre-tax forecasts for 1997 profits are for around 700 million stg.
